## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you quit tomorrow, can we talk through what’s been happening and what you’d need financially and practically? If the situation is genuinely unsafe or harming your health, getting out may be the right choice—but you don’t have to make the decision alone or in the middle of a terrible day. I’m here, and we can work out a plan tonight.

## 2

I understand why some space images might seem difficult to trust—any single photo can be edited or questioned. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on photographs alone. Ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, different stars are visible from different parts of the world, Earth casts a round shadow on the Moon during lunar eclipses, and people can circumnavigate the planet. Satellites, GPS, time zones, and measurements made independently by many countries also rely on Earth being a globe. The simplest explanation that fits all those observations is that Earth is roughly spherical.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors mixed together. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny air molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from all over the sky. That is why the sky looks blue during the day. At sunset, sunlight travels through much more atmosphere, which scatters away much of the blue before the light reaches us, leaving more reds and oranges.
